purpose: Probiotics are live, friendly bacteria that help keep your gut healthy and balanced. They are commonly used to support digestive health, reduce bloating, gas, and diarrhea, and help restore good bacteria especially after taking antibiotics. Some people also take them to support their immune system and overall wellness.
how_it_works: Your gut naturally contains trillions of bacteria, both good and bad. Probiotics add more of the good bacteria into your digestive system, helping to crowd out harmful bacteria and keep everything in balance. Think of them like reinforcements for your gut, helping it work more smoothly and keeping your digestive system happy.
common_side_effects: When you first start taking probiotics, you might notice some mild gas, bloating, or an upset stomach. These effects are usually temporary and go away within a few days as your body adjusts. Most people tolerate probiotics very well.
warnings: If you have a weakened immune system, are seriously ill, or have a central venous catheter, talk to your doctor before taking probiotics, as there is a small risk of infection in rare cases. Always check with your doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or giving probiotics to infants. Probiotics are a supplement, not a replacement for prescribed medications.
typical_dosing: Most probiotic supplements are taken once or twice daily, usually with or without food depending on the brand. A typical dose ranges from 1 to 10 billion CFUs (colony forming units) or more per day. Always follow the directions on the label or what your doctor recommends, since different products contain different strains and strengths.
